5 Stars | A Hidden Gem for Indian Food Lovers in Saigon!
Apr 2025 • Couples
Sri Natraj Restaurant at Bui Xuan is a true culinary oasis in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City. As someone who’s picky about Indian food abroad, I was genuinely impressed.

I ordered the Butter Chicken and Kabuli Channa with Pranthas and every bite was packed with rich, authentic flavors. Perfectly spiced, hearty, and comforting — just like home. The food wasn’t just good, it was remarkably consistent and soulful.

The ambience strikes the perfect balance between cozy and elegant, making it a great spot for both casual dining and special evenings. The staff was warm, attentive, and knew the menu inside out.

It’s no surprise that Sri Natraj has won the TripAdvisor Travellers’ Choice Award every year since 2017 — and after this experience, I can see why. Truly well-deserved.

Highly recommend this place to anyone craving real Indian food in Saigon — whether you're a tourist or an expat, this place is a must-visit.

Roermond, The Netherlands89 contributions

Excellent food. Friendly and very tasty.
Aug 2023 • Family
We went here for dinner on the advice of our guide. And we are not disappointed, on the contrary!
We were welcomed by very friendly staff. The menu is quite extensive, so choosing was difficult because it all seemed delicious.
Finally started with both vegetarian and chicken samosa as a starter. Delicious, including the red sauce.
Main dishes (paneer masala, chicken masala and something else I forgot) were also great. We chose the medium spicy version and it was delicious and not too spicy.
We also ate rice and garlic naan bread. Delicious.
We would like to eat here again and explore the menu further.
The only minor point of attention was the “lime juice”. We had better ones in Vietnam.
But all in all: great! Recommended!

Surprisingly good food
Mar 2023 • Couples
My hubby ordered chicken dahiwala, with garlic naan and jeera rice. I ordered a masala dosa with masala on the side.

The hubby thoroughly enjoyed his food because for the past four days, we had been struggling to find food to fit our palette. 

The masala of my masala dosa was yum, but the chutney was tasteless and the dosa didn't have the same consistency associated with dosa.

We also ordered samosas for appetizer and they were tasty.

Overall, the place is clean, nicely decorated, has a bar, and is well-lit (I like to see my food when I eat it, lol). 

All in all, I recommend this place if you'd like to enjoy a good Indian meal at good prices and with friendly service.

Authentic Indian in Saigon
Nov 2022 • Family
My family and I spent 10 days in Vietnam and our 3rd stop was Ho Chi Minh City. We stayed at the Eden Hotel and were looking for something nearby to eat. We are from the south side of Chicago and Little India is way up north so we don't get it that often. What a treat this place is! A word of warning, if you don't like spicy food make sure to order it mild, they are not lying when they label the items spicy. My favorite item was the Mutton Curry (spicy) and my girlfriend's was the vegetarian samosas. The rice was not too oily and the Naan was crisp and well seasoned. Get the bread basket so you can try all the different Flatbreads especially if you get a Curry. This has been our favorite place all trip!

Leean W

Most Deicious Indian Restaurant in Saigon
Oct 2019 • Couples
I had read many very good reviews of this restaurant but took it with a pinch of salt as I know how the reality can often disappoint but the food here is truly superb. This is the first time I had a byriani that was identical to the byrianis in the UK, dry and flavoursome without being saturated with curry sauce having been mixed in like other Indian restaurants in Vietnam. The chicken was also very good - none of this manky slippery chicken sometimes found elsewhere. The manager was also very accomodating. I asked if I could just have a bowl of Vindaloo sauce to add to the byriani which was immediately agreed to. The Vindaloo was super tasty and exactly the spiciness you would expect from Vindaloo - very spicy without being inedible like a Phall spiciness. The Chicken Kadai was probably the best I have ever eaten anywhere and was exactly the correct medium spiciness. It was rich and delicious. The accompanying pappadoms were fried and cooked to perfection and all of the complimentary sauces were excelent. But particular mention must be made of the home made green mango chutney. It was heavenly! The garlic nan was just normal. There is a bit of a down side to this restaurant though because although the food is definitely deserving of a 5 star rating, on each of the 3 occasions I have gone there we have been the only customers. But maybe because it was early evening, although quite a few people popped in for a takeaway and the delivery man was back and for constantly. Also- the manager is lovely- very warm, welcoming and friendly. But he would do well to remind his waiters to occasionally smile or return a smile or greeting to the customers as one or two of them have very offputting manners. That said, it still remains the most tasty Indian restaurant in town.

Fantastic food
Aug 2019 • Couples
Went to this lovely quaint restaurant with my wife this evening being 3rd August 2019.
Bizarre having an Indian meal in Vietnam you may say,but I went with my wife's wishes and I'm so glad I did. 
Greatly by a waitress very smiley and welcoming. 
The manager then came over and explained about to dishes and how hot they were, he was attentive and warm. 
We had poppadoms and onion bargie as starter with 3 accompanying condiments. 
For main my wife had chicken kadhia and I had keema mutton,and a boiled rice to share was plenty for 2. As well as 2 nan bread 2 waters and 2 tiger beers, all for just over 580,000.dong.
This has to be one if not the best keema mutton I have had and my wife absolutely loved her chicken. 
The whole meal and experience was lovely and the prices are excellent for the quality of the food. 
Try for YOURSELF. We will deffinately recommend this to friends who visit Vietnam from the U. K. 
We will certainly make a return visit if we can. 
Thank you for a lovely evening. 

Pd. Epsom. England u.k

reviews.review_title: Review at Natraj Indian Cuisine Restaurant
reviews.review_text:
ChefSaraP
Glendale, Arizona26 contributions
0
A hidden gem!
Jul 2017 • Couples
We happen to come upon this Indian restaurant across from our hotel the same day we arrived. As we pass by it, the intoxicatingly delicious aromas of Indian spices hit my senses and left me feeling light headed with desire for Indian food, and made my mouth water! However, we already had something planned so I just peeked at their menu outside to see the selections they offer. As the restaurant's door opened and closed from so many customers coming in and out which is very promising and a very good sign, my craving for Indian food became intense from that delicious aromas wafting in the air and surrounding me. I knew right there and then, just from the aromas that their food will be awesome and made a mental note to make sure and eat there the following days. 

Boy was I wrong! The food at Natraj Indian Cuisine Restaurant is not by any means awesome, it's spectacular!!! I kid you not, it's the best Indian food I've ever had! And trust me, as a Culinary graduate from Le Cordon Bleu in Scottsdale, AZ and as a Chef, I am qualified to rate their food and I know what I'm talking about. The last time I had a spectacular Indian dish was when our Sous Chef at the Phoenician Hotel prepared our family meal, and he's from Goa, India. He cooked the food in secrecy protecting his own recipes from prying eyes, such as mine. To this day, I dream of that dish he made and I couldn't find another one like it nor can I duplicate it --- it must be some secret ingredients I have yet to uncover! 

Then, Natraj Indian Cuisine Restaurant happened 3 days ago! We ordered chicken tikka masala, mutton Dahiwala, rice, and garlic Naan bread. Boy, that naan bread after we took one bite of it and we were ordering a second one! We could have had dinner with just the naan bread and the sauces in our dishes and forego the rice all together! But, the chicken and mutton in our dishes are to die for, as well. They're moist, tender, and succulent! They were both cooked to perfection and nothing but, bathe in this sauce that I would say made for the Gods! The flavors on the sauce is perfectly, perfectly, balanced with just the right amount of heat to tickle the back of your throat, the spices blended so well and cleanly without it being muddled, that it makes you want to keep eating. 

As I try to dissect what seasonings and ingredients are in the sauce that's familiar to my palate, I taste a hint of cassia bark, fenugreek, cloves, cardamom, cumin, coriander, nutmeg, mace, turmeric, mustard seeds, and peppercorn. They're the usual and common spices in Indian cooking, but, there's one, there's something in there that I can taste and I'm familiar with but I can't quite place it and it's eluding me. It also reminds me of the same thing that my Sous Chef back in Phoenician has in his dish that he ever so protectively hid from me. As I wallow in bewilderment of that one elusive ingredient, I continued to devour every morsel and drop of sauce in our dishes, short of licking the dish itself! Yeah, it was that good that I was very tempted! 

As our dinner comes to an end, the Chef came out and I told him how fabulous and how much we thoroughly enjoyed his food. He smiled from ear to ear and spend a good 15 to 20 minutes of his time talking to us about his food and food in general. Well, lo and behold, he whispered to our ears that one ingredient that has eluded me for years! I have actually come very, very, close to discovering it myself for I have used something very similar to it but not quite it, and that makes a huge difference in flavor! He also gave me some secret techniques and uses of the ingredient, similar to converting a mother sauce to become another sauce. All I could say was wow, and my head is spinning from hundreds of possibilities I can make with that one ingredient not just in my Indian recipes, but, with my Mediterranean, Peruvian, Middle Eastern, Thai, and other numerous Asian cuisines! I left the place feeling happy, content, very inspired, and couldn't wait to create magical dishes with that one ingredient! 

I know that you would want to know that one ingredient he whispered to my ears, but, out of respect to the Chef of Natraj Indian Cuisine Restaurant and the restaurant itself, I'm afraid I can't reveal it to you for it is not mine to give. It is up to the Chef and the Chef alone if he wants to share it with you, when you come and visit Natraj Indian Cuisine Restaurant. We are going back for dinner there tonight so we can try his other dishes with Naan of course, and I'm sadden with the fact that it's our last night here in Hoi hi Minh. We haven't left and yet, I'm missing his food already. He surely have set the bar higher for me, and I'm sure that it would be hard press to find a restaurant in the U.S. that would remotely come close to his fabulous food. Yes, it's that good and I'm hoping that I can come close when I make it.

second, i am so jaded to the no smiles faces in many establishments, so it was great to see a couple of smiley "indian" greeting me:) the wait staff is efficient, they can use a few smiles to not be so mechanical:))

finally, the presentations were done well, with shiny clean spotless water glasses, spotless silverwares, and the light is about right so i can see the gleam in the cleanliness of the place (i prefer it a wee bit lower in the dining area:)

the prices are fair for indian restaurants in the area:) i feel fair about it:) for what wonder time i had eating juicy mutton curry with jeera rice, some dal fry, with fresh chopped garlic, minced ginger, more lime... and then some:)) in my excitement i forgot to ask for fresh onion:)) i brought the leftover home because the curry will taste even better tomorrow:))

even better, i ordered a mutton biryani to go, the kitchen told me it is dum biryani:) the package now sits in the fridge, well done, i am a happy happy person:)) i don't recommend any places to anyone anymore:) i just tell of my experience of the place and it is up to friends to go there if they choose to:)) sometime i bring friends along too:)) my two year old daughter like natraj too:)))

Best INDIAN restaurant in town
May 2016 • Couples
I and my wife came here for dinner last week. We've tried almost famous Indian restaurnt in HCM City, and BABA KITCHEN was the best of them. But BABA made me down on the last time I went there, so we were looking for a different one. We use voucher of hotdeal, it consist of 3 dishes:
- Indian Milk tea : Very good. It had a unique flavour, and I'm absolutely sure you wouldnt be able to find in another restaurnt. Try it, you wont regret !
- Vegetarin Samosa : as good as BABA
- MUTTON curry : we didnt know which kind of curry was in the voucher, cause there is a dozen of mutton curry in the menu !!! It's good, authentic, on the same level with BABA
- Garlic naan and cheese naan : I ate a awful garlic naan at BABA , and NATRAJ's probably the best. Cheese naan was good too.
- Indian rice : Believe me Natraj offer you the best Indian rice you can get in HCM City. I'd always abandonned Indian rice before, but now I can say that Indian rice is delicious ( only at Natraj)
- Sweet soup : The same in every idian restaurant
